diagnostic_evidence.quote: The mapping $F:\widehat{D}_h\rightarrow D$ is invertible, and let $F^{-1}$ denote the inverse of $F$. Then there holds
Denote the identity mapping as $id$ and the auxiliary mapping $\Phi_h = F_h\circ F^{-1}:D\rightarrow D_h$, respectively

issues.failure_explanation: The mesh $\mathcal{T}_h$, the space $V_{h,k}$ (defined via $F_h^{-1}$), the map $\Phi_h^{-1}=F\circ F_h^{-1}$ and hence $f_h$, $g_h$, $I^\dag$ and the discrete problem (2.4) all presuppose that the degree-$k$ interpolant $F_h$ is a bijection $\widehat D_h\to D_h$. Only $F$ is assumed invertible ($(H_3)$). Local invertibility of $F_h$ follows from (2.1) and $(H_2)$ ($\|\mathbb I-\mathbb J_{F_h}\|\lesssim h$), but global injectivity of a piecewise degree-$k$ map on a possibly nonconvex polyhedral domain is a nontrivial fact (established by degree-theoretic arguments in Lenoir 1986 / Arnold–Walker 2020, cited here only as construction references) and is neither assumed nor proved.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the global invertibility of $F_h$ (for $h$ sufficiently small) as an explicit hypothesis, or prove it via the standard degree-theoretic argument for interpolated boundary transformations.
issues.overall_effect: If $F_h$ is not injective, elements of $\mathcal{T}_h$ overlap, $V_{h,k}$, $\Phi_h^{-1}$, $f_h$, $g_h$, $I^\dag$ are ill-defined, and the DG scheme (2.4), Lemma 2.1 and the entire error analysis of Section 3 lack well-defined meaning.
issues.title: Global invertibility of the interpolated mapping F_h is tacitly assumed
issues.why_classification: The gap is filled by a standard known result; adding it as an assumption or cited proposition changes no claim, rate, or advertised scope.

issues.failure_explanation: Bounding $L_4$ by Cauchy–Schwarz requires $\||\Omega\cdot n_h|^{1/2}(\tilde I-\Lambda\tilde I)^-\|_{L^2(\partial_-K/\Gamma_h)}\lesssim\|\tilde I-\Lambda\tilde I\|_{DG}$. The DG norm controls only the $\sigma$-weighted $L^2$ norm, traces on $\Gamma_h$, and jumps $\llbracket\cdot\rrbracket$ on interior faces — not one-sided traces on interior faces, which is what $w^-=(\tilde I-\Lambda\tilde I)^-$ is. The step is therefore not 'straightforward', and (3.4) fails as a uniform statement: an admissible extension $\tilde I\in H^{k+1}\cap W^{1,\infty}$ with thin layers concentrated along element faces has small $L^2$ norm and small jumps but $O(1)$ face traces, making $L_4/(\|w\|_{DG}\|v_h\|_{DG})$ arbitrarily large.

failure_location.quote: From the definition of the DG norm, applying Cauchy-Schwarz inequality and the boundedness of $\sigma$, it is straightforward to observe that $L_1 + L_3 + L_4 \lesssim \|\tilde{I} - \Lambda\tilde{I}\|_{\mathrm{DG}} \|v_h\|_{\mathrm{DG}} .$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Weaken (3.4) to $\mathcal B(\tilde I-\Lambda\tilde I,v_h)\lesssim h^{k+1/2}\|\tilde I\|_{H^{k+1}(\mathcal T_h)}\|v_h\|_{DG}$, bounding the trace of the projection error on faces by the standard $h^{k+1/2}$ estimate (the same tool as in (3.3)); Theorem 3.1 then follows unchanged, since its right-hand side already contains $h^{k+1/2}\|\tilde I\|_{H^{k+1}}$.
issues.overall_effect: Lemma 3.2 is unproven and false as stated; the step (3.19) in the proof of Theorem 3.1, which invokes Lemma 3.2 to bound $\mathcal B(\tilde I-\Lambda\tilde I,\,\Lambda\tilde I-I_h)$, is unsound, so Theorem 3.1's proof does not stand as written.
issues.title: Lemma 3.2: the bound of L_4 by DG norms is unjustified (one-sided interior traces are not controlled by the DG norm)
issues.why_classification: The stated lemma is false and must be replaced by a weaker comparable estimate, with a contained additional trace argument; no global proof architecture is needed and the main theorem's rate and scope survive.

issues.failure_explanation: Composition with a near-identity map is not Lipschitz in $L^2$ with constant equal to the displacement: the mean-value argument gives $\|\tilde I-\tilde I\circ\Phi_h^{-1}\|_{L^2}\lesssim h^{k+1}\|\nabla\tilde I\|_{L^2}$, i.e., a bound with $\|\tilde I\|_{H^1}$, exactly the pattern used correctly for gradients in (3.10) with $H^2$. Consequently the first term of (3.8) with only $\|\tilde I\|_{L^2}$ cannot hold uniformly: an oscillatory $\tilde I$ with fixed $L^2$ norm makes $\|\tilde I-\tilde I\circ\Phi_h^{-1}\|_{L^2}=O(\|\tilde I\|_{L^2})$ while $h^{k+1}\|\tilde I\|_{L^2}\to0$. Lemma 3.3 as stated is false; moreover the final line of (3.11) also drops the resulting $h^{2k+1}\|\tilde I\|_{H^1}^2$ contribution.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace $\|\tilde I\|_{L^2(\mathcal T_h)}$ by $\|\tilde I\|_{H^1(\mathcal T_h)}$ in (3.8) and prove it via the mean-value argument (as done for the gradient in (3.10)); Theorem 3.1 is unaffected since $h^{k+1/2}\|\tilde I\|_{H^1}\le h^{k+1/2}\|\tilde I\|_{H^{k+1}}$ for $k\ge1$.
issues.overall_effect: Lemma 3.3 is false as stated, and the bound of $T_1$ in the proof of Theorem 3.1, which is taken 'directly' from Lemma 3.3, is unsupported as written.
issues.title: Lemma 3.3: invalid L2 shift bound (3.9); the claimed estimate with only $\|\tilde I\|_{L^2}$ is false
issues.why_classification: A labelled estimate is false and must be weakened (the $L^2$-norm claim is withdrawn and replaced by an $H^1$-norm), with a routine but non-typo correction of the proof; the downstream theorem survives fully.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: 0 is the regular value of the function $f(x) = \Omega\cdot \boldsymbol{n}_h(x)$, that is, $\forall x\in f^{-1}(0)$, $\nabla f(x)\neq 0$
Under the shape-regularity and quasi-uniformity of $\mathcal{T}_h$, the total length of the discrete zero level set remains bounded independently of $h$

issues.failure_explanation: Two failures. (i) The hypotheses do not exclude $\Gamma$ containing an open patch everywhere tangent to $\Omega$ (e.g., a cylinder with axis parallel to $\Omega$, or in 2D a straight side parallel to $\Omega$). On such a patch $\Omega\cdot n\equiv0$ and the isoparametric normal error gives $|\Omega\cdot n_h|\lesssim h^k$ with oscillating sign; 0 can still be a regular value of $f=\Omega\cdot n_h$ (transversal crossings of the oscillation), so $(A_1),(A_2)$ hold while $T_{h^k}$ contains the entire patch and $\mathrm{Area}(T_{h^k})=O(1)\gg h^k$: the lemma is false. (ii) Even in the nondegenerate case the proof is incomplete: the bound $\sum_F \mathrm{Length}(\Gamma_F^0)\lesssim1$ is asserted from shape-regularity/quasi-uniformity, but per-face algebraic length bounds over the $\Theta(1/h)$ faces crossed by the characteristic curve only give $O(h^{-1})$; an $O(1)$ bound requires a confinement argument (via (3.14)) plus a uniform lower bound on $|\nabla(\Omega\cdot n_h)|$ near the zero set, which follows only from a transversality assumption on the exact boundary that is never made.

failure_location.quote: Then the area of the set $T_{h^k} = \{ x \in \Gamma_h : |\Omega\cdot \boldsymbol{n}_h(x)| \lesssim h^k \}$ satisfies $\mathrm{Area}(T_{h^k}) \lesssim h^k$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add a nondegeneracy assumption on the exact characteristic boundary, e.g., $|\nabla_\Gamma(\Omega\cdot n)|\ge c>0$ on $\{x\in\Gamma:\Omega\cdot n(x)=0\}$ (no open tangency patch), and complete the confinement/length argument using (3.14); Lemmas 3.4–3.6 and Theorem 3.1 then hold. (Alternatively, degenerate tangency requires a new analysis; note (3.17) itself also follows directly from (3.14) and the sign argument in Lemma 3.5's proof.)
issues.overall_effect: Lemma 3.4 is unreliable, so Lemma 3.5's area bound (which fails in the same admissible geometry), Lemma 3.6's distance-based proof of (3.17), and the $T_3$ estimate in Theorem 3.1's proof all break; Theorem 3.1 is not established on the full scope its hypotheses advertise.
issues.title: Lemma 3.4 is false under its stated hypotheses (boundaries with patches tangent to $\Omega$) and its proof has gaps
issues.why_classification: A limited weakening — excluding tangential-patch geometries, a nongeneric degeneracy — plus a contained completion of the proof preserves the rate, the method, and the generic scope; no source-supported repair covers the degenerate regime itself, but the result remains recognizably comparable.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Assume that there exist two positive constants $m$ and $M$ such that $0<m\leq\sigma\leq M$.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof repeatedly passes from $L^2$ norms to DG norms (e.g., from (3.7) to (3.4) inside Lemma 3.2, and in the assembly of $E_1$ and $T_3$), which is valid only if $0<m\le\sigma$: with $\sigma\equiv0$ the DG 'norm' is only a seminorm (a piecewise polynomial that is continuous across faces and vanishes on $\Gamma_h$ has zero DG norm but positive $L^2$ norm). Theorem 3.1 assumes only $(H_1)$–$(H_3)$ and $(A_1)$–$(A_2)$; the model problem introduces $\sigma$ merely as 'a bounded absorption coefficient', and $0<m\le\sigma\le M$ is assumed only in Lemma 2.1.

failure_location.quote: Suppose that the assumptions $(H_1\sim H_3)$ and $(A_1\sim A_2)$ hold. Then for any $k\geq 2$, there holds

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the standing hypothesis $0<m\le\sigma\le M$ (as in Lemma 2.1) to Theorem 3.1.
issues.overall_effect: As stated, Theorem 3.1 covers absorption coefficients (including $\sigma\equiv0$) for which the DG norm is not a norm and its proof's norm equivalences fail.
issues.title: Theorem 3.1 omits the positive lower bound on $\sigma$ that its proof needs
issues.why_classification: Adding this standard local condition (already assumed for the scheme's stability in Lemma 2.1) is a short, local fix that preserves the method, conclusion, rate, and the intended scope of the theory.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let $f_h\in W^{1,\infty}(\mathcal{T}_h)$ and $I_h$ be the numerical solution of (\ref{eq2.4}).

issues.failure_explanation: The pointwise bound $|\tilde f(x)-\tilde f(\Phi_h^{-1}x)|\le h^{k+1}\|\nabla\tilde f\|_\infty$ requires $\tilde f$ to be Lipschitz along the segments from $x\in D_h$ to $\Phi_h^{-1}x\in D$, which cross the mismatch band $D_h\setminus D$ where $\tilde f$ takes extension values. The hypotheses give only $\tilde I\in W^{1,\infty}$ (hence $\tilde f\in L^\infty$, no bound on $\nabla\tilde f$) and $f_h\in W^{1,\infty}$ (which controls $f$ on $D$ only); the regularity of the extension on the hold-all region is an unestablished premise. The final bound (3.18) is stated with $\|f_h\|_{W^{1,\infty}}$, which does not control $\tilde f$ on $D_h\setminus D$.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Assume the extension is chosen $W^{1,\infty}$-stable for $\tilde f$ (a Lipschitz extension of $f$ to the hold-all $D_H$, or $\tilde I\in W^{2,\infty}$), which is standard for Lipschitz domains, and state the theorem accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: The $E_1$ term of the consistency error, and with it the proof of Theorem 3.1, rests on an unestablished regularity of the extension $\tilde f$.
issues.title: The $E_1$ estimate uses $\|\tilde f\|_{W^{1,\infty}}$, which the hypotheses do not supply
issues.why_classification: A one-clause strengthening of the (analyst-controlled) extension hypothesis fills the gap; no conclusion, rate, or scope changes.

issues.failure_explanation: $D_c$ (the boundary elements intersected by the characteristic set $\Gamma_h^0$ or its $h^k$-tube) consists of $\Theta(1/h)$ elements in 3D (resp. $\Theta(1)$ in 2D) of size $h$, so $Vol(D_c)=\Theta(h^2)$, which is not $\lesssim h^{k+1}$ for $k\ge2$: a surface region of area $h^k$ spread along the $O(1)$-length characteristic curve touches $\Theta(1/h)$ whole elements, so an 'area times one layer thickness' volume bound is fallacious. The cited justification, Eq. (3.8), is Lemma 3.3's solution-error estimate and has no bearing on mesh-region volumes. With the correct $Vol(D_c)\sim h^2$, the displayed chain yields only $T_3\lesssim h^{k}\|\tilde I\|_{W^{1,\infty}}\|v_h\|_{DG}$, half an order short of the claimed $h^{k+1/2}$, so the proof does not close.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Re-derive the $T_3$ bound using Lemma 3.5's surface-area estimate directly: $\|\tilde I\|_{L^2(\Gamma_h^-\setminus\Phi_h(\Gamma^-))}\le\|\tilde I\|_{L^\infty}\mathrm{Area}^{1/2}\lesssim h^{k/2}\|\tilde I\|_{W^{1,\infty}}$ and $\|v_h\|_{L^2(\cdot)}\lesssim h^{-1/2}\|v_h\|_{DG}$ via the trace inequality, giving $T_3\lesssim h^{(3k-1)/2}\le h^{k+1/2}$ for $k\ge2$; the theorem's conclusion is preserved.
issues.overall_effect: The $T_3$ estimate (3.25), and hence the proof of Theorem 3.1, is unsound as written.
issues.title: Proof of Theorem 3.1: false claim $Vol(D_c)\lesssim h^{k+1}$ (with an unrelated citation) breaks the $T_3$ estimate
issues.why_classification: A false, load-bearing intermediate claim must be replaced by a different (sharper) contained argument; the final result, rate, and scope are preserved, but the correction is a replacement argument rather than a forced typo fix.
